page: Microsoft Azure D8ns_v6 is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dnv6 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The configuration provides 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 4.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware acceleration flags such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

This server does not include local storage, though it is premium storage capable, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses. In benchmark evaluations, the D8ns_v6 demonstrates average performance across most standard workloads. Its stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance scores are 1900.68 and 7619.12, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 591.47 GB/sec, which drops to 64.69 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write speed of 44.7 GB/sec. The PassMark CPU score is 13504.19, and the database operations benchmark registers at 4873.67.

The hardware demonstrates varying capabilities in machine learning and data processing. For small-scale language model inference using a 135M model, text generation reaches a strong tier at 279.99 tokens/sec, while prompt processing sits at an average 772.22 tokens/sec. However, scaling to a medium 7B model reveals a performance tradeoff, with text generation dropping to a weak tier of 8.08 tokens/sec. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 10.46 million operations/sec, and static web serving throughput reaches 14.07 GB/sec. This profile makes the instance suitable for general-purpose computing, network-optimized routing, web serving, and lightweight database operations.
